title: NASA's Saturn fact sheet: mean density 687 kg/m^3 and 274 satellites
summary: The sheet lists Saturn's mass as 568.32 × 10^24 kg, mean density 687 kg/m^3, equatorial radius at the 1-bar level 60,268 km, sidereal orbit 10,755.699 days, and 274 natural satellites.
body: The sheet lists Saturn's mass as 568.32 × 10^24 kg, mean density 687 kg/m^3, equatorial radius at the 1-bar level 60,268 km, sidereal orbit 10,755.699 days, and 274 natural satellites. It lists a planetary ring system as Yes. Density below 1000 kg/m^3 is the sheet's figure for the planet as a whole. The satellite count is the count printed on this dated sheet. Author of the sheet: Dr. David R. Williams, NASA Goddard Space Flight Center. Last updated on the page: 2025-03-18.
